inputs.share_count_basis: 619,346k shares outstanding net of treasury at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin; ties to Q1 EPS 134.33 = 83,194/619.3) x 2 for the 2-for-1 split effective October 2026 (Yahoo split event 2026-09-28) = 1,238,692k. The Yahoo price is post-split, so the divisor must be too. Held flat: SBC is immaterial (director restricted stock only) and there is no non-SBC issuance programme; FY2025 buyback (Y87.1bn) was the last repurchase.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 consolidated balance sheet (Q1 FY2027 tanshin): short-term loans 1,051,469 + current bonds 91,000 + current LT loans 167,337 + commercial paper 250,000 + bonds 663,000 + LT loans 1,241,148 = 3,463,954; cash and bank deposits 459,663. Hybrid loans/bonds (50% equity credit from rating agencies) are counted as debt in full. Finance-lease obligations (Y6bn/yr principal, inside 'other liabilities') excluded, consistent with J-GAAP lease treatment below. Net debt swings seasonally: 31 March 2026 was 2,642bn; the Q1 inventory build (+Y205bn real estate for sale) is funded with short-term paper. Using the latest observation per the vintage rule; the seasonal swing is ~Y290/share and is noted so a reader can see it.
inputs.fcf_note: No full-year FY2026 (Mar-2026) consolidated cash flow statement exists in the English extracts (only the tanshin summary and the results presentation were published in English for Q4). last_fcf is therefore the latest full year available: FY2025 (Mar-2025) OCF 420,561 less total investing outflow 493,370 = -72,809 (Integrated Report 2025 financial highlights, line 6330-6331). Total investing (not gross PPE capex alone) is the right FCF measure for this company because development property bought as PPE is reclassified to 'real estate for sale' before disposal, so proceeds show in OCF as an inventory decrease while the outlay sat in investing. H1 FY2026 (Sep-2025): OCF -79,183, PPE/intangibles capex 226,901 -> -306,084, driven by a Y219bn inventory build. SBC is zero and interest income is not inside EBITDA, so owner FCF = reported FCF here.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market. Integrated Report 2025 remuneration section (lines 5402-5454): only directors receive restricted stock / performance-linked transfer-restricted stock; there is no employee equity programme and no share-based payment line in the consolidated cash flow statement. Annual cost is well under Y1bn against Y5.6tn revenue; charged at 0% and kept visible as its own line per house rule.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income ~Y5bn/yr and dividend income ~Y10bn/yr sit in non-operating income, outside the EBITDA the flows are built from, so nothing is stripped. The matching assets: cash is in net debt; investment securities (Y309bn) are in the equity bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 (Mar-2026): Y7m in H1, none material in the year. FY2025 (Mar-2025): Y87.1bn. The flat count is a convention that the FY2026 cash flows did not fund; dividends (~Y108bn/yr at Y175 pre-split DPS) were debt-funded alongside reinvestment.
inputs.fy0_note: CSV label FY2026 = fiscal year ended 31 March 2026, which the company itself calls 'FY2025'. All company-labelled years in the Analysis JSON are one lower than the CSV labels used here. Guidance for the year ending March 2027 (CSV FY2027 / company FY2026) is year 1 of the projection.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketPrice at 02:30Z = 11:30 JST, an intraday print at the Tokyo lunch break, not a close; replace at the next regular close. 52-week range 2,040.5-2,902.5 (split-adjusted).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free 2.0% (10y JGB, BOJ policy rate 1.0% and rising), ERP 6.0%, beta 1.0 -> cost of equity 8.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt 2.0% (Q1 FY2027 interest expense Y13.2bn/qtr on Y3.46tn is 1.5% today; marginal fixed-rate issuance is higher), 31% tax -> 1.4% after tax. Weighted at management's own target structure of D/E ~0.6x (D/V 37.5%), not today's 0.98x: 0.625 x 8.0 + 0.375 x 1.4 = 5.5%. At current market weights (D/V 54%) the same inputs give 4.4%; at the house ~9% JPY industrial reference the business is unlevered and net-cash, which Daiwa House is not. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, BOJ risk and integration risk are charged in the flows, once.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating income (the lease cost is already in EBITDA), and the small finance-lease book (Y6bn/yr principal repayments, Sep-2025 CF statement line 779) is excluded from net debt. One treatment, leases-as-operating-cost; lease_cost_pct_path is not used because the charge is already inside the margin. Japan's new lease standard (ASBJ No. 34, mandatory from fiscal years beginning April 2027) will capitalise operating leases from year 2; when it does, EBITDA and debt rise together and this treatment must be re-stated, not stacked.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (EBITDA includes subsidiaries with minority holders, e.g. US homebuilders with management stakes and Sumitomo Densetsu/SEMLINKS until fully squeezed out). NCI is therefore deducted once, in the equity bridge, at the 30 June 2026 book value of Y93,041m. Profit attributable to NCI was Y864m in Q1 FY2027, so book value is a fair proxy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (margin and reinvestment intensity are both still moving at year 5). Daiwa House is an operating company -- construction contracting ~63% of sales, recurring leasing/management ~33%, development-property sales ~6% -- not a REIT or a pure land subdivider, so the routing table's operating-company row applies, with the non-US adaptations (JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases, NCI, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero). The inventory-heavy developer row was considered and rejected as the primary model because property-for-sale is one of three revenue models and the group is 95% operating business; its lesson is kept as a memo (see supplementary_views.nta_floor): on the bear path the flows-only value falls below the Y2,349/share of book equity, which is the asset floor this engine does not credit. DATA GAP: the English integrated reports FY2017-FY2025 omit the full cash flow statement, so annual capex and FCF are absent from the CSV for those years. The gap is bridged from (i) the Integrated Report 2025 nine-year financial highlights, which carry OCF, investing CF and financing CF for every year (lines 6330-6332), (ii) the interim cash flow statements H1 FY2024-FY2026 (gross PPE+intangibles capex 189.5 / 173.5 / 226.9bn per half; D&A 56.7 / 63.5 / 68.2bn), and (iii) 9M D&A kpis (103.9bn to Dec-2025, Q1 FY2027 36.5bn run-rate). Derived: D&A ~2.5% of revenue, gross capex ~7-8%, total investing (incl. M&A) ~7% of revenue on average, OCF ~6%. ACTUARIAL GAIN: FY2026 reported operating income Y614.8bn includes Y115.6bn amortisation of pension actuarial differences (non-cash, from the FY2024-25 rate-driven pension surplus; the company reports and pays dividends on the ex-actuarial figure). The margin paths are anchored to the underlying Y499.2bn (8.95% EBIT, ~11.5% EBITDA), not the reported figure. The CSV's FY2026 net income of 271,439 is also the ex-actuarial figure; reported attributable net income was Y350.5bn. STOCK SPLIT: 2-for-1 effective October 2026; all per-share values here are post-split. Pre-split equivalents are 2x. GUIDANCE: year ending March 2027 -- net sales ~Y5.8-5.9tn (+4-6%), operating income Y400bn ex-actuarial (Y460bn incl.), explicitly framed by management as a conservative COVID-like emergency scenario after the Middle East shock; the 8th Medium-Term Plan was withheld in May 2026. Q1 FY2027 actuals (sales +9%, operating income +10.6%) are running well ahead of that guidance; year-1 base margin sits between the guidance margin (9.3% EBITDA) and FY0 underlying (11.5%). PENSION: the Y236bn pension asset less Y97bn liability (net surplus ~Y139bn) is deliberately NOT added to the bridge -- it is the source of the actuarial gains already stripped, is not distributable, and partly offsets the long-tail nature of the construction-warranty and asset-retirement provisions.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities at balance-sheet value (listed holdings at fair value, affiliates incl. Alliance Residential stake at equity)
equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 tanshin, consolidated balance sheet 30 June 2026 line 440. Their dividend income (~Y10bn/yr) is non-operating and outside the flows, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule). No tax haircut applied; the unrealised gain in OCI is Y67bn, so a 31% haircut on it would be ~Y17/share.
Q1 FY2027 tanshin line 494, 30 June 2026. Flows are fully consolidated, so NCI is deducted here and nowhere else.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8.2% / 9.6%) exceeds revenue CAGR (4.4% / 6.2%) by well over 30%. The gap is not organic: retained earnings include non-cash actuarial-gain amortisation (Y115.6bn in FY2026 alone), FX translation gains on the US business added Y163bn to equity, and ROE of ~12% is produced by D/E ~1.0x on an unlevered return of ~6%. Equity CAGR is therefore rejected as the growth anchor in favour of revenue.
historical_growth.notes: CAGR bases (CSV labels; year ended 31 March): revenue FY2023 4,908,199 -> FY2026 5,576,861 (3yr) and FY2021 4,126,769 -> FY2026 (5yr). EPS uses reported attributable EPS on the pre-split count: FY2023 469.12, FY2021 297.18 -> FY2026 ~565 (350.5bn / ~620m; the CSV FY2026 EPS cell is empty and its net income is the ex-actuarial 271.4bn). Shareholders' equity ex-NCI FY2023 2,284,213 / FY2021 1,835,197 -> FY2026 2,896,744. Owner FCF CAGRs are undefined: the series (OCF + investing CF, Integrated Report 2025 highlights) is -56.0, +68.7, +41.6, -167.6, +40.3, -131.0, -274.9, -8.1, -72.8 bn for FY2017-FY2025 and -306.1bn for H1 FY2026 -- the company has reinvested every yen of operating cash flow and more for a decade. That, not the growth rate, is the valuation question: revenue grew Y2.06tn FY2017-FY2026 on ~Y4.0tn of added debt and equity, an incremental return on capital of ~3.5-4% pre-tax-adjusted, below any JPY WACC.

owner_fcf_history.basis: OCF + net investing CF (includes M&A and property investment; development property passes through PPE into inventory before sale, so gross capex alone overstates the reinvestment and OCF alone understates it). Millions of JPY, CSV fiscal-year labels (year ended 31 March).
owner_fcf_history.source: 1925.T_Annual_FY2025.txt lines 6330-6331 (Integrated Report 2025 financial highlights); H1 FY2026 from 1925.T_HalfYear_H1-2025.txt lines 726-757

base.growth_note: Year 1 at 5.0%: guidance is Y5.8-5.9tn (+4-6%) on a self-described emergency scenario and Q1 FY2027 printed +9%; 3yr revenue CAGR is 4.35%. Decelerates to 1.5% as Japanese housing starts (816k, down from 987k in FY2014; houses sold 32k vs 55k peak) shrink structurally and US homebuilding growth matures.
base.margin_note: Underlying (ex-actuarial) EBITDA margin: FY2025 ~10.5%, FY2026 ~11.5%. Year 1 at 10.5% sits between the 9.3% implied by the Y400bn ex-actuarial operating-income guidance and FY0; recovers to 11.5% by year 7 as logistics/data-centre construction mix and recurring revenue (33% of sales, +29% over the 7th Plan) offset condominium and single-family pressure. No margin expansion beyond FY0's level is assumed.
base.da_note: 9M FY2026 D&A 103,911 on 4,030,292 revenue = 2.58%; Q1 FY2027 36,482 on 1,408,385 = 2.59%. Rises slightly as the leased-asset base (Y2.36tn PPE) grows faster than contracting revenue.
base.capex_note: Gross PPE+intangibles capex ran 7-8% of revenue in FY2025-FY2026 (H1 173.5bn / 226.9bn) and total investing CF averaged ~7% of revenue FY2017-FY2025 including M&A. Base assumes management's stated need to bring D/E from 0.98x toward ~0.6x produces partial discipline: 6.0% in year 1 (Sumitomo Densetsu is closed, no comparable deal assumed) gliding to 3.8% at maturity -- D&A 2.7% plus ~1.1% growth capex, consistent with 1.5% terminal growth at the group's ~1.0x capital/revenue intensity.
base.wc_note: Negative capture: a developer-contractor consumes cash as it grows. Net operating working capital (real estate for sale 2,415 + in process 853 + receivables 517 + construction costs 78 - payables 328 - advances 394) is ~Y3.1tn, 56% of revenue, and the ratio has risen with the US land bank (75,017 lots). -35% of incremental revenue assumes the intensity of new growth falls to ~2/3 of the stock ratio as land-banking is reined in. This is the single most consequential driver after capex.
base.tax_note: Japan statutory effective rate ~30.6% plus the defence surtax taking effect from fiscal 2026 -> 31%. Cash taxes paid H1 FY2026 Y98.6bn on H1 pre-tax Y207.5bn (47%, timing) and FY2015 Y77.2bn on ~Y190bn; no NOLs or structural shelters are disclosed.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 5.5%/1.0% would be 22.4x terminal FCF; capped at 16x because the business is cyclical (interest rates, land prices, corporate capex) but a third recurring. 16x FCF with FCF ~73% of NOPAT is ~11.7x NOPAT, roughly 7.5x EBITDA versus 9.2x underlying EV/EBITDA today -- the cap assumes a modest de-rating, not expansion.

bull.narrative: Capital discipline plus the data-centre pivot. Management treats the 0.98x D/E as the binding constraint, holds gross investment near Y350bn, recycles development property to the Daiwa House REIT and institutional buyers faster (WC capture -25%), and lets FCF emerge. SEMLINKS (Sumitomo Densetsu) electrical contracting plus Module DPDC data-centre construction and semiconductor-fab work lift the construction mix; US deliveries climb toward 10,000 homes on the 75k-lot bank with Sun Belt demand intact; recurring revenue passes Y2tn. Margins reach 12.5% EBITDA (10% underlying EBIT), a level the 7th Plan touched only with actuarial gains. Terminal multiple 18x FCF: still below a mature compounder's 20x.

bear.narrative: The guidance scenario turns out to be the real one, then rates bite. Year 1 lands on management's Y400bn ex-actuarial operating income (9.3% EBITDA margin); the BOJ moves to 1.5-2.0%, Japanese single-family and condominium demand falls with mortgage rates and the US housing cycle rolls over together, taking revenue down 1-2% for two years and compressing margins to 8.5%. Reinvestment does not fall as fast as revenue (the land bank and the leasing pipeline are committed), so FCF stays negative through year 4 and D/E drifts above 1.0x; interest cost on Y3.5tn re-prices from 1.5% to ~2.5%. Recovery from year 5 is to a 10% EBITDA margin, below FY0. On this path the flows-only equity value sits at or below zero; the Y2,349/share of book equity (mostly Y3.3tn of real-estate inventory and Y2.4tn of PPE) is the asset floor the DCF does not credit, and the realistic bear outcome is a capital raise or a forced disposal programme at a discount to book rather than a wipe-out.

scenario_narratives.base: Daiwa House keeps compounding revenue at 3-5% near term, fading to 1.5%, on a flat-to-FY0 underlying EBITDA margin of ~11.5%, while partially honouring its own leverage target: gross investment falls from ~7.5% of revenue to ~3.8% over seven years and inventory intensity of new growth drops to about two-thirds of today's stock ratio. The result is owner FCF that is roughly zero in year 1 (as it has been for a decade) and ~Y320bn by year 10. The valuation is then a question of what a buyer pays for a Y320bn FCF stream from a cyclical, 1.0x-levered developer-contractor in a 1.5%-growth economy; at 16x the equity is worth materially less than the Y2.9tn market capitalisation, because ~Y3.0tn of net debt sits ahead of it. The market is paying book value (P/B ~1.0, P/E ~10.7 underlying) and, implicitly, assuming reinvestment earns its cost of capital; the ten-year record (incremental ROIC ~3.5-4%) says it has not.
scenario_narratives.bull: As in assumptions.bull.narrative: capital discipline is enforced by the D/E constraint, development property recycles faster, SEMLINKS and data-centre/semiconductor construction lift the mix, US deliveries scale on the land bank, and the underlying EBITDA margin reaches 12.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: As in assumptions.bear.narrative: the COVID-like guidance scenario is realised, BOJ tightening and a US housing downturn coincide, revenue falls for two years, reinvestment lags, and the flows-only equity value falls to or below zero against a Y2,349/share book floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: D/E is 0.98x against a 0.6x target with the BOJ hiking (rate sensitivity is high on both the customer side and Y3.5tn of debt), the 8th Medium-Term Plan was withheld in May 2026 so there is no multi-year management commitment to test against, management itself framed FY2027 on an emergency scenario, and the ten-year record shows reinvestment returns below WACC -- the bear is the continuation of history plus a cycle, not a tail. Bull cut to 20%: it needs capital discipline, margin expansion to a level never achieved ex-actuarial, and US housing to hold through a rate cycle, three independent things going right. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict basis for Japan's largest diversified homebuilder-contractor-developer: cash flows built from underlying (ex-actuarial) EBITDA through 31% cash tax, D&A, gross investment and working-capital consumption, discounted at a JPY WACC built on the company's own target capital structure, with the terminal value capped at a cyclical multiple. Investment securities are added and minorities deducted once in the bridge; leases follow J-GAAP (expensed, excluded from debt); SBC is zero and the house/street band collapses. The central finding is about reinvestment, not growth: for ten years Daiwa House has reinvested all of its operating cash flow and funded dividends with debt, earning roughly 3.5-4% on the incremental capital. A DCF that charges that history values the equity well below the book value the market is paying; the gap between the model and the price is the market's bet that the D/E constraint forces discipline (the bull case) or that leverage at 1.5% JPY debt is a permanent source of value (an implied WACC of ~4.4%). Both are stated as scenarios rather than baked into the base. A supplementary NTA memo is included because, on the bear path, the flows-only model falls below the asset floor and understates what equity holders would actually recover.
key_risks_to_valuation: Reinvestment intensity (capex_pct_path and wc_capture_pct) is the dominant driver: each 1pp of terminal capex/revenue is worth ~Y450/share; if management does not reduce gross investment from ~7.5% of revenue, owner FCF never becomes positive and the equity value on a flows basis is near zero in every scenario
Net debt of Y3.0tn (June 2026) is 1.0x market capitalisation, so every Y100bn of EV moves the equity ~Y80/share; the seasonal Q1 debt peak (vs Y2.64tn at March) is itself ~Y290/share

Terminal multiple: Gordon at 5.5%/1.0% is 22x and the 16x cap binds; at 20x the base case rises roughly a quarter. The cap is a judgment that a cyclical, levered developer does not get a compounder's multiple

JPY WACC is built at the 0.6x target D/E; the market-weight WACC is ~4.4% and the house industrial reference is ~9% -- the valuation is highly rate-sensitive in both directions, see the sensitivity grid

FY2026 full-year cash flow statement is absent from the English extracts; the capex and FCF anchors are interim and prior-year figures, and the actuarial-gain split relies on the company's disclosed ex-actuarial operating income
The 2-for-1 split (October 2026): all values here are post-split on 1,238.7m shares; a reader comparing with pre-split broker targets must halve them
BOJ policy (1.0% and rising) hits both mortgage demand and the ~Y55bn/yr interest bill; the new J-GAAP lease standard from April 2027 will restate EBITDA and debt

Integration of ~Y292bn Sumitomo Densetsu/SEMLINKS, three US homebuilders, Alliance Residential and the European modular business concurrently with a two-headquarters reorganisation and a CEO/COO split

nta_floor.note: The routing table's inventory-heavy-developer row would blend an NTA exit-P/B with an earnings exit-P/E. That is not the primary model here (Daiwa House is 95% operating business), but it is the right lens for the bear case: Y3.3tn of real estate for sale and Y2.4tn of PPE at historical cost back the Y2.9tn of book equity, so the flows-only bear value (at or below zero) is a statement about cash generation, not about recoverable value. The market price is almost exactly book.

market_implied.note: P/E on FY2026 underlying attributable income Y271.4bn (ex-actuarial, Y219/share post-split) and reported Y350.5bn (Y283/share). EV/EBITDA on underlying operating income 499.2bn + D&A ~140bn = ~639bn.
